elements.content: Grammar focus: Cohesion, Ellipsis & Lexical Substitution.

Core Rule: Use cohesive connectors ( notwithstanding, subsequently, accordingly ) and substitution markers ( do so, the former / the latter ) for elegant discourse continuity.

Cohesive Connectors — notwithstanding / subsequently / accordingly: Notwithstanding initial setbacks, the venture secured funding.
Substitution (Nominal) — the former / the latter: The report analyzed solar and wind energy; the former showed higher growth.
Substitution (Verbal) — do so / doing so: If members wish to vote, they must do so in writing.
Guided practice: choose the correct option.
1. Choose the sentence that correctly uses verbal substitution:
options: Should you wish to submit an application, please do so before Friday.
Should you wish to submit an application, please submit application before Friday.

elements.content: 2. In 'We reviewed Option A and Option B; the latter was selected', what does 'the latter' refer to?
Read and listen: three examples in context.

the former (prioritized cost efficiency, while the latter emphasized rapid expansion.)
did so (promptly.)
1. Function check: What is the primary purpose of using Cohesion, Ellipsis & Lexical Substitution?
options: To express clear, level-appropriate meaning in structured context
To translate sentences word-for-word from another language
It is an obsolete form never used by native speakers

elements.content: 2. Form check: Does correct usage of Cohesion, Ellipsis & Lexical Substitution require matching subject, verb, and modifier agreements?
options: No, agreement rules are optional in English
Yes, matching grammatical forms ensures natural, accurate communication
Agreement only matters in formal academic writing

Success criteria:

- Substitute repeated VP structures with 'do so' or 'doing so'
